Rio Ngumoha is going to be a 'wow' player for Liverpool - and he demonstrated everyone exactly what he is already capable of in Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United.

He made an outstanding assist then added a fine finish, and there is much more to come. He plays without fear so he is going to score and make many more goals the same way.

Ngumoha has only just turned 18 but he is already a game-changer, someone who gets people excited because he is so hard to stop when he is one-on-one.

Of course he can frustrate you at times too, but that's what creative and explosive wingers like him do - and it's because he is so talented that everyone wants to see an end product from him every time he gets on the ball.

There were times against United when Ngumoha did not quite deliver, but he is still so young and I would much rather see players like him take too many touches - or try too many things and fail - than be afraid to try them in the first place.

So, if he runs out of play or runs into too many players at times, because teams are doubling up on him like United were, that just demonstrates how scared they are of him.

His ability means he occupies opposition players - Youri Tielemans was always backing up Diogo Dalot on his wing to try to help him out, but that just meant United were leaving someone else free.

Ngumoha stars as Liverpool thrash 10-man Man Utd.

Sometimes it is actually harder when you are playing out wide against 10 men because you don't get the same amount of space - United were not attacking the same way they would have done with 11, and they were sitting in more.

Yes, Ngumoha ran up the odd blind alley or got outnumbered but that is always going to happen. As he learns, and gets even better, his decision-making will improve too. He will know when to try to go past people or when to find that free man instead.

But he still highlighted all the bravery you want from a winger against United and, when you keep trying things the way he did, something is going to come off for you.

I look at Bradley Barcola in a similar way to Ngumoha - he can be frustrating but he tries things, and can be brilliant.

For Liverpool right now, one of the biggest positives is the competition they have in wide areas, with those two plus Victor Munoz and Cody Gakpo.

There are other areas of their squad, like left-back or central midfield, where that competition needs to improve, but I don't really worry about the wide attacking areas in the same way.

Sunday was only Ngumoha's second Premier League start of the season, and his first since the opening day.

He maybe only got his chance because Gakpo has a calf problem but, when everyone is fit, it is really exciting that they will all be thinking they have to play their best to push the manager and get in the team.

Andoni Iraola post-match interview - Liverpool v Man Utd.

It has been revealed that there were plenty of other positives for Liverpool, too. All in all, Sunday could not have gone much better for them.

United made a woeful start with poor concentration and mistakes which cost them but, from there, Liverpool saw the game out well.

Just because the opposition has a man sent off early on does not mean any kind of victory is a given, let alone a 4-0 win.

Look at how United's 11 men lost to City's 10 in the Manchester derby earlier this season - we've seen many times how good teams can frustrate a side with an extra player like that.

It definitely does not mean you are going to steamroller them, but Liverpool did that and made an abundance of chances to get even more goals.

Days like this are so vital for building belief in all their attacking players, especially because they were playing at home, and against their big rivals.

Up until now, it had felt like Liverpool's better days this season had come on the road, but now the pressure and expectation is off them a bit - particularly if, like Ngumoha or Florian Wirtz, you have scored and played well.

Industry observers note that I know from experience that, the next time they go back to Anfield, they will be buzzing. You know that the fans are already with you after you've scored against United, and you feel the love a little bit more.

This is the start of a big week for Liverpool and Iraola will probably make changes against Club Brugge in Belgium on Wednesday, knowing how difficult Sunday's Merseyside derby will be.

Everton is always a tough game but I think Liverpool will enjoy their trip to Hill Dickinson Stadium, and the confidence they will have after beating United will mean they can go there with a really positive mindset.

Breaking: I got to tour SpaceX's Starfactory facility in Starbase, Texas, and what I saw blew my mind

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1374 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

💡 Key Takeaways
  • STARBASE, Texas  — I just finished covering the Starship Flight 15 mission, and SpaceXs incredible launch tower catch of the returned Ship 42 spacecraft isn't the only thing over the weekend that left me speechless.
  • 13), SpaceX invited media on a tour of Starbase's Starfactory facility, where it manufactures and assembles both stages of its massive Starship rocket - an unprecedented behind-the-scenes look at the production and scale of SpaceX's operations, and a glimpse of things to come as Starship notches more and more milestones the more it flies.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

STARBASE, Texas  — I just finished covering the Starship Flight 15 mission, and SpaceXs incredible launch tower catch of the returned Ship 42 spacecraft isn't the only thing over the weekend that left me speechless.

The morning of the launch (Nov. 13), SpaceX invited media on a tour of Starbase's Starfactory facility, where it manufactures and assembles both stages of its massive Starship rocket - an unprecedented behind-the-scenes look at the production and scale of SpaceX's operations, and a glimpse of things to come as Starship notches more and more milestones the more it flies.

For some context, the five-story-tall Starfactory spans approximately 1 million square feet (~93,000 meters), with operations split between Starship's Super Heavy boosters and upper stage Ships, and nearly 330,000 additional square feet (30,000 square meters) of office space. SpaceX officials describe its design as one more akin to an automotive manufacturing plant than that of a typical aerospace production site, and inside, it is absolutely alive with activity.

Recent findings suggest that we entered through an arch-covered doorway underneath the giant "X" sign on the building's shorter face. Our media gaggle was met with curious glances as we were shown through the doors and guided onto the factory floor - few are ever able to cross that threshold outside of SpaceX employees, and our presence seemed as novel to those busy working as it was to us.

Industry observers note that inside, we were struck with the sheer enormity of Starship's scale. Giant stainless-steel rocket parts were meticulously scattered across different subassembly stations throughout the building, with Ship nose cones, cylindrical sections and booster components all under various stages of manufacture. The sheer quantity of the hardware was staggering, and being so close to each as we walked Starfactory's throughways was an eye-opener.

Starbase is a unique partnership of privately-owned SpaceX property and publicly-accessible land and shoreline, which has created the unique ability for anyone with a mind to do so to drive right up to the the Starship launch pad to see the facilities up close (within a few hundred feet or so, which, as rockets go, is very, very close).

In a recent development, fully stacked, Starship stands more than 400 feet (120 meters) tall. Standing next to such a towering colossus on the pad is enough to drive home just how major the launch vehicle is, but standing next its segmented components inside Starfactory is even more humbling; like seeing one of Ship's upper aerodynamic flaps, which are each large enough when laid flat that you could park a pair of large SUVs on their faces with room to spare.

Starbase, Texas https://t.co/NqDWwUZXv9August 25, 2025.

It has been revealed that as our tour continued and we passed rows of nose cones under preparation for integration, numbering as high as Ship 51, one stood out from the others. In the distance, only visible for moment between the overlapping views of other Ships as we walked through the production stations, was a nose cone with a series of windows cut out of its face - undoubtedly a prototype for, or possibly even the final article that will be used as NASA's Artemis lunar lander.

According to recent reports, NASA has contracted SpaceX to develop a version of Starship capable of landing astronauts on the moon as a part of the agency's Artemis program, and this appeared to the Ship being readied for when that mission arrives. NASA is targeting Artemis IV as the program's first crewed lunar landing in 2028, and while the decision solidifying Starship as the lander tasked with that mission isn't finalized (Blue Origin is also vying for that spot with its Blue Moon lander), SpaceX is clearly operating with the intention of coming out ahead.

But Artemis is clearly not SpaceX's only focus, as evident by the many, many other Ships in production that did not have window holes carved out of them.SpaceX officials said the manufacturer is currently completing about one Ship upper stage every two weeks, and one Super Heavy booster every four weeks, with overlapping production allowing multiple rockets to move through the factory simultaneously. The majority of the vehicles currently being assembled will carry stacks of SpaceX's upgraded Starlink Version 3 (V3) satellites.

It has been revealed that the company's Starlink network in low Earth orbit at the moment consists of more than 11,000 spacecraft beaming wireless internet to SpaceX customers across the globe. All of those were introduced on SpaceX's workhorse Falcon 9 rocket, with the exception of a few more than 50 delivered on Starship's two most recent test flights. Both carried V3 Starlink stacks to add to the constellation, which SpaceX officials say each added the data capacity equivalent to ten Falcon 9 Starlink debuts. And, as they fine tune Starship's design, SpaceX prepares to increase the vehicle's launch cadence dramatically, growing the Starlink network as it does.

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has stated the firm hopes to launch Starship about once a week beginning in 2027, and with the number of Ships we saw lined up inside Starfactory, launch vehicle inventory doesn't seem like it will be to blame if that goal isn't realized.

SpaceX has adopted a manufacturing process modeled after the automotive industry, where efficiency and reproduction allow for the manufacture of large numbers of identical parts. Automation is a critical part of that process, but not one SpaceX is ready to entirely rely on.

According to recent reports, much of the equipment and tools being used for Starship's production were designed by SpaceX engineers, who are constantly refining production processes to eliminate bottlenecks. And SpaceX has deliberately kept technicians on the floor as Starship's design continues to evolve, rather than automating procedures that might soon become obsolete.

Our tour guide compared SpaceX's manufacturing consistency goals to that of Lego bricks, which are famously precise in their production down to the micro-millimeter accuracy of what now number more than 1 trillion bricks made since the toy organization began in the 1940s.

Exiting the far side of the building, we stood in the shadow of SpaceX's two towering Mega Bays, where the sections of Starship are stacked and integrated with their engines - there's one hanger for Ship, and another for Super Heavy. Each can hold about five or six assemblies, and housed two or three vehicles at the time our tour was brought by.

Both Mega Bays, however, looked small against the adjacent Gigabay SpaceX is at the moment constructing. At approximately 700,000 square feet (65,000 square meters), Gigabay will be equipped with room to accommodate up to 24 vehicles at a time, and will facilitate a major increase in SpaceX's ability to assemble its Ship and Super Heavy rockets.

In a recent development, part of SpaceX's goal with Starship is to make all of what we got to see completely routine; to make rocket launches and landings as ordinary as commercial airline flights. Still, standing inside Starfactory, surrounded on all sides by huge spacecraft in various stages of assembly, it was hard to imagine a reality where giant rockets flying to and from space on a regular basis wouldn't feel like science fiction.

Later that day a giant rocket launched to outer space - Super Heavy did attempt a return to pad, but was diverted for an offshore landing instead, where it exploded. But the next day, Ship 42 came plunging through the overcast cloud cover, falling belly-first toward the same tower it left just a couple dozen hours before. And then it lit its engines and was caught by the tower.

That felt like science fiction too.

Josh Dinner is Space.com's Spaceflight Staff Writer and a photographer with a passion for science and exploration. He has worked the space beat since 2016, covering the evolution of NASA's commercial spaceflight partnerships and crewed missions, planetary science missions, the Artemis program and humanity's return to the moon. He also enjoys building 1:144-scale model rockets and spacecraft. Find some of Josh's launch photography on Instagram, and follow him on X, where he mostly posts in haiku.

Ngumoha stars as Liverpool thrash 10-man Man Utd.

"Sacked in the morning, you're getting sacked in the morning...".

Fourteen minutes in, arms folded, two goals down at Liverpool and with his Manchester United team reduced to 10 men, Mauricio Pochettino could not ignore the cruel taunts echoing around Anfield.

What on earth must Pochettino have been thinking as he stood at the edge of his technical area?

In distance terms, he was 3,800 miles from his last managerial assignment against Haiti in Cincinnati in the early hours of Wednesday morning UK time.

In difficulty levels, it must have felt significantly further than that.

By the final whistle, as Liverpool's gleeful supporters alternated between singing about the notion of Pochettino's immediate dismissal, United "going down" and celebrating "Poch is at the wheel", the Argentine head coach would have been starting to understand the scale of the task he has taken on by quitting his United States job.

He had just watched United be dismantled 4-0 by their oldest rivals, with Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card and two quickfire goals soon after representing just about the worst possible start imaginable to his reign as manager.

His team sit 19th in the 20-team Premier League after 11 games, already 20 points behind leaders Arsenal.

"Animals of the grass, we like to smell it and feel it," was the memorable phrase Pochettino came out with during Friday's pre-match media conference, explaining how he has missed the day-to-day nature of club football.

Listen to former United skipper Roy Keane's post-match summary of the loss on Sky Sports and a very different smell comes to mind.

For the record, it was the joint-worst result for any new United boss, matching the 4-0 loss Lal Hilditch suffered against Bolton in October 1926.

Hilditch lasted 30 games and never managed another team.

Pochettino endures nightmare start as Man Utd lose to Liverpool.

The red card that changed Liverpool-Man Utd: correct call?

Yoro sees red as Ngumoha shines - Liverpool v Man Utd player ratings.

Liverpool run riot for Pochettinoâs nightmare debut.

Keane is not one for holding back, so his response to his old side's latest setback was predictable.

Recent findings suggest that "Fans are applauding the players [at the end]. Applauding what? Applauding rubbish," he said. "When do the players take responsibility for some of the decision-making?".

There were enough images of chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox broadcast during the game by Sky Sports to suggest there is a wider debate to be had about the quality of the players at Pochettino's disposal.

Recent findings suggest that on Friday, Berrada stated this season's squad was "fundamentally better" than the one which finished third last season. Few would agree with that, and presumably Keane is among the group who would challenge Berrada's assertion.

Pochettino, 54, shed tears of emotion when he explained his difficulty in deciding to quit the United States job and take up an opportunity at a club he has flirted with for the best part of a decade but, only now, has been given the chance to coach.

It was easy to imagine him being reduced to tears again as Sunday's debacle unfolded, a nightmare afternoon in Liverpool coming at the end of a chaotic week of travel.

He arrived to begin his latest role as United head coach on Wednesday after agreeing a two-and-a-half-year contract.

The USA beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati in his final game in charge on Tuesday, with Pochettino flying directly to Manchester on a private jet after the game. He landed at about 11:30 GMT before heading to the club's Carrington training ground - and his feet have barely touched the floor since.

Mauricio Pochettino gives his post-match verdict on Liverpool v Man Utd.

Pochettino was bullish when speaking to the media after this 4-0 defeat.

Although he began his first answer by saying he went to referee Sam Barrott after the final whistle to "present his respect", he became increasingly more forceful in his view Leny Yoro should not have been sent off.

After dismissing the sorry statistic that United have conceded 19 goals in their latest six games, because he didn't want to talk about results and performances that occurred before he replaced Michael Carrick, he then used Yoro's red card as the prism through which his side's entire performance at Anfield should be judged.

"What I learned from my players [today] is that they like to fight. They are committed with the team, with the club, and of course they want to win games," Pochettino said.

"Today we made an unbelievable effort. Today was a test. After eight minutes, 10 men, red card, concede the goal in this action. Do you think that is easy?

"Even the best team in the world playing like this in this situation, in our circumstance, maybe concede the four goals or maybe more.".

Man Utd shouldn't worry about relegation, yet - Young.

Industry observers note that it is a basic truth that Pochettino won six games this season as United States boss, twice as many as United have managed in 16 matches across all competitions. His latest team have kept one clean sheet, against Azerbaijanis Sabah FK in the Champions League in September.

Pochettino's biggest selection call was to alter his defence by handing Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in almost 12 months.

It was a De Ligt misread of a bouncing ball that led to Yoro having to decide whether to foul Alexander Isak before he entered the penalty area.

"It was clearly a foul and he was clearly the last man," noted home boss Andoni Iraola, giving his reading from a Liverpool perspective. "Will he score? We will never know.".

Pochettino had a different opinion.

"If you go a minute and a half before, [Jeremy[ Jacquet and [Bryan] Mbeumo and compare it..." he mentioned, suggesting his team should have been awarded an earlier penalty.

"Yes, it's painful because it's 4-0. But for us to play 80 minutes with 10 men is unfair. We need to be critical but the action of Liverpool [player] was also a mistake, no? But we were punished and they were not. That is the truth.".

Pochettino takes his team, and his grievance, to Lisbon on Wednesday for a Champions League encounter with Sporting.

Industry observers note that after that, it is Brentford, Newcastle and Coventry in the Premier League. This, to an extent, was a game United and their fans, and even Keane probably, expected little from.

If they are still in the relegation zone after Coventry have left Old Trafford on 5 December, United really are in trouble.

#127946. Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1268 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that an eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function.
  • Recent findings suggest that the findings suggest that the amount of time children spend in front of screens may be less notable than how they use that time.
  • The discovery comes amid growing concerns about insufficient physical activity among teenagers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that an eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function. Researchers found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the widespread assumption that screen time is necessarily harmful to developing brains.

Recent findings suggest that the findings suggest that the amount of time children spend in front of screens may be less notable than how they use that time. Activities that encourage learning, creativity, and problem-solving could be particularly valuable. Researchers emphasize that the goal should not be to eliminate screen time, but to balance it with physical activity and mentally stimulating experiences.

The discovery comes amid growing concerns about insufficient physical activity among teenagers. A sedentary lifestyle has been linked to poorer academic performance, while regular exercise is known to support brain function, particularly in adults. However, scientists still have much to learn about how physical activity, sitting, and screen use during childhood influence thinking abilities later in adolescence.

It has been revealed that these questions are especially important because childhood and adolescence are critical periods of brain development. Changes in attention, memory, and learning during these years can have lasting consequences, potentially influencing educational opportunities and career paths well into adulthood.

To investigate these relationships, Finnish researchers examined how screen time, physical activity, and sedentary behavior from childhood through adolescence were associated with cognitive performance in teenagers. They also explored whether the connections differed between boys and girls and whether the intensity of physical activity made a difference.

More Screen Time Linked to Better Thinking Skills.

One of the study's most unexpected findings was that greater screen time throughout childhood was associated with better cognitive processing in adolescence.

Cognitive processing refers to the mental abilities people use to take in information, pay attention, remember details, learn latest things, and solve problems. These abilities play an important role in school performance and everyday decision-making.

It has been revealed that the findings challenge the idea that all screen time should be viewed as harmful. However, the researchers caution that the relationship may depend on what children are actually doing while using digital devices. Watching videos, playing games that require strategic thinking, and engaging in educational activities may involve very different levels of mental effort.

Recent findings suggest that "The findings suggest that screen time can support children's and adolescents' cognitive processing. Presumably, the essential point here is what kind of things they do in their screen time. Teachers and parents should encourage children to use devices and screens in such ways that promote active thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and learning," states Doctoral Researcher Petri Jalanko from the University of Jyväskylä.

"We should not regard screen time solely as harmful but seek balance between physical activity and screen time that promotes active thinking," Jalanko summarizes.

Exercise Affects Boys' and Girls' Brains Differently.

The researchers also uncovered a more complicated picture of how physical activity relates to thinking and memory.

Among girls, spending more time engaged in light-intensity physical activity since childhood was associated with better working memory during adolescence. For boys, greater participation in guided physical activity over the same period was linked to stronger working memory.

Industry observers note that working memory is the brain's ability to temporarily hold and use information. It allows someone to remember instructions while completing a task, keep track of numbers during mental calculations, or follow a conversation while processing new information.

Light-intensity physical activity generally includes relatively gentle movements that do not substantially increase breathing or heart rate. Guided physical activity refers to exercise carried out with some form of instruction or supervision, such as organized sports or structured exercise sessions.

Recent findings suggest that the differences between boys and girls suggest that the relationship between exercise and brain health may depend on more than simply how much a person moves. The type of activity, how it is organized, and the individual's sex could all play a role.

Another Surprising Finding About Physical Activity.

The study produced another counterintuitive result. Teenagers who reported spending less time in unsupervised physical activity tended to perform better on measures of cognitive processing.

Yet when researchers used wearable sensors to objectively measure movement and heart rate, they found no association between overall physical activity or sedentary time and cognitive performance.

According to recent reports, one possible explanation is that wearable devices measure movement without revealing what a person is actually doing. For example, a sensor may record periods of sitting or physical activity, but it cannot determine whether someone is solving a difficult problem, studying, participating in an organized activity, or simply resting.

This distinction could help explain why questionnaire responses revealed relationships that were not apparent in the sensor measurements.

"Our study indicates that the connections of physical activity and sedentary behavior to cognitive processing are complex and depend on the sex, the type and assessment method of physical activity and sedentary time. Moreover, boys and girls may benefit from different types of physical activity in view of brain health," Jalanko adds.

In a recent development, "However, we need more intervention studies to find out causal relations and sex differences in this respect. Moreover, it is key to examine more specifically the effects of the intensity of physical activity on changes taking place in cognitive processing.".

What the Eight-Year Study Revealed.

The findings come from an eight-year follow-up conducted as part of the PANIC study, a long-running Finnish research project investigating children's physical activity and nutrition.

The current analysis included 260 participants, consisting of 124 girls and 136 boys. Their average age at the adolescent assessment was 15.8 years.

Sources indicate that researchers collected information about physical activity and sedentary behavior using both questionnaires and wearable devices that combined heart rate monitoring with movement measurements. This approach allowed them to compare participants' reported activities with data collected by sensors.

To evaluate cognitive abilities, the researchers used the CogState test battery, a collection of computerized assessments designed to measure aspects of mental performance. The tests examined learning, attention, and working memory.

According to recent reports, importantly, the findings show associations rather than cause and effect. They do not establish that increasing screen time will improve a child's thinking abilities or that reducing certain types of exercise will produce cognitive benefits. Intervention studies, in which researchers deliberately change participants' activities and measure the results, are needed to determine whether these relationships are causal.

Nevertheless, the results offer an key perspective on the continuing debate over children's screen use. Rather than treating all time spent with digital devices as equally harmful, the researchers suggest paying closer attention to whether those activities encourage active thinking and learning.

The research also highlights the importance of considering different forms of physical activity rather than focusing exclusively on the total amount of exercise children receive.

Together, the findings suggest that supporting healthy brain development may require a more nuanced approach, one that combines physical activity with opportunities for learning, creativity, and mental engagement, including those that take place on screens.

The study was published in the scientific journal Pediatric Exercise Science.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, three men are vying for one of the most powerful positions in sports when delegates from more than 200 member nations of FIFA, soccer's global governing body, cast their ballots at the FIFA presidential election, to be held in Rabat on March 18, 2027.
  • Gianni Infantino was first elected FIFA president in February 2016, promising greater transparency and a fresh start in the wake of the corruption scandals that marked the Sepp Blatter era.
  • Recent findings suggest that during his decade in office, the 56-year-old Swiss has built a global network of support.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, three men are vying for one of the most powerful positions in sports when delegates from more than 200 member nations of FIFA, soccer's global governing body, cast their ballots at the FIFA presidential election, to be held in Rabat on March 18, 2027. DW looks at the field of candidates.

Gianni Infantino was first elected FIFA president in February 2016, promising greater transparency and a fresh start in the wake of the corruption scandals that marked the Sepp Blatter era. Under Infantino's leadership, FIFA's revenues have continued to grow, the Club World Cup has been revamped, and the men's World Cup has been expanded to include 48 teams.

Recent findings suggest that during his decade in office, the 56-year-old Swiss has built a global network of support. Infantino enjoys significant backing in Africa, South America, and large parts of Asia — a result of multi-billion-dollar development programs and financial grants provided to national associations. Many smaller member associations view him as a president who takes their interests more seriously than his predecessors did.

According to recent reports, at the same time, critics accuse Infantino of consolidating power within the organization around himself. During his tenure, oversight and control bodies have been restructured multiple times, and key positions have been filled with his own loyalists.

Infantino's ostentatious closeness to political leaders has also sparked debate — whether exemplified by his conduct during the World Cup in Qatar, his tight ties to Saudi Arabia or his public appearances alongside US President Donald Trump (though that relationship is mentioned to have cooled significantly after the 2026 World Cup). Detractors accuse him of seeking proximity to authoritarian rulers and intermingling political interests too closely with football.

It has been revealed that A failed initiative to grant private investors a larger stake in lucrative FIFA competitions (FIFA Forward Enterprise) has also placed Infantino under considerable pressure. As the FIFA election approaches, he faces the prospect of legal challenges; European football's governing body UEFA is aiming to take action over the investment plan, while other critics are calling for an investigation by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

According to recent reports, however, his time in office has brought many of FIFA's 211 member associations additional development funding and other revenue. This makes him the man to beat in the March vote.

Philippe Diallo is Europe's candidate. The 63-year-old, who was elected president of the French Football Federation in 2023, is seen as an experienced sports administrator with a pragmatic and measured leadership style.

He has the backing of UEFA, as well as many of its 55 member associations, including the German Football Association (DEB).

"Philippe Diallo stands for a version of football that embraces responsibility and tackles future challenges with determination," DFB President Bernd Neuendorf said in a statement announcing the German FA's position.

"We want a FIFA that serves the sport in the interest of all its member associations. That is why we support Philippe Diallo with great conviction.".

Diallo is positioning himself as a clear alternative to Infantino. His supporters see him as a candidate who stands for sound leadership, transparency, and a stronger dialogue with member associations. Unlike the incumbent, however, he lacks a global network of allies.

The third man in the race is Kozo Tashima. The 68-year-old was president of the Japan Football Association (JFA) from 2016 to 2024 and has been one of the most influential officials in Asia for decades.

During a press conference in the Japanese capital Tokyo on Friday, Tashima mentioned the words "integrity, fairness, trust and transparency" several times in explaining his decision to run.

"I just don't only want to be the FIFA president, my intention is to make FIFA better," he said.

"Being the president is the shortcut to making that happen. I just want to clean up the federation and make it a fair organization. I want to help rebuild the whole organization.".

Tashima also acknowledged that failing to have won the endorsement of any of the regional confederations — the Asian Football Confederation is supporting Infantino — makes him a longshot to win the election.

According to recent reports, but he could still play a key role in the outcome. At a press conference on Tuesday, Diallo stated he intended to reach out to Tashima to "unite forces" to defeat Infantino. Tashima hasn't ruled out the notion.

"We do share some moral or ethical positions, so he's a great person to team up with," he remarked.

"Diallo is also very strict in governance and he does have a lot of experience in management," he added.

However, Tashima also noted that he hadn't had any thoughts of withdrawing from the race.

If Infantino's challengers do manage to join forces in some way, they might just stand a chance of upsetting the highly favored incumbent.

The haunting Masters meltdown that changed Rory McIlroy's career

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Editor’s Note:  This story was originally published in April 2023.
  • Slumped on his club, head buried in his arm, Rory McIlroy looked on the verge of tears.
  • The then-21-year-old had just watched his ball sink into the waters of Rae’s Creek at Augusta National and with it, his dream of winning The Masters, a dream that had looked so tantalizingly close mere hours earlier.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Editor’s Note:  This story was originally published in April 2023.

Slumped on his club, head buried in his arm, Rory McIlroy looked on the verge of tears.

The then-21-year-old had just watched his ball sink into the waters of Rae’s Creek at Augusta National and with it, his dream of winning The Masters, a dream that had looked so tantalizingly close mere hours earlier.

As a four-time major winner and one of the most decorated names in the sport’s history, few players would turn down the chance to swap places with McIlroy heading into Augusta this week.

Yet on Sunday afternoon of April 10, 2011, not a golfer in the world would have wished to be in the Northern Irishman’s shoes.

A fresh-faced, mop-headed McIlroy had touched down in Georgia for the first major of the season with a reputation as the leading light of the next generation of stars.

An excellent 2010 had marked his best season since turning pro three years earlier, highlighted by a first PGA Tour win at the Quail Hollow Championship and a crucial contribution to Team Europe’s triumph at the Ryder Cup.

Yet despite a pair of impressive top-three finishes at the Open and PGA Championship respectively, a disappointing missed cut at The Masters – his first at a major – served as ominous foreshadowing.

McIlroy shot 74 and 77 to fall four strokes short of the cut line at seven-over par, a performance that concerned him enough to take a brief sabbatical from competition.

But one year on in 2011, any lingering Masters demons looked to have been exorcised as McIlroy flew round the Augusta fairways.

Having opened with a bogey-free seven-under 65 – the first time he had ever shot in the 60s at the major – McIlroy pulled ahead from Spanish first round co-leader Alvaro Quirós with a second round 69.

It sent him into the weekend holding a two-shot cushion over Australia’s Jason Day, with Tiger Woods a further stroke behind and back in the hunt for a 15th major after a surging second round 66.

Industry observers note that and yet the 21-year-old leader looked perfectly at ease with having a target on his back. Even after a tentative start to the third round, McIlroy rallied with three birdies across the closing six holes to stretch his lead to four strokes heading into Sunday.

Recent findings suggest that the youngster was out on his own ahead of a bunched chasing pack comprising Day, Ángel Cabrera, K.J. Choi and Charl Schwartzel. After 54 holes, McIlroy had shot just three bogeys.

“It’s a great position to be in … I’m finally feeling comfortable on this golf course,” McIlroy told reporters.

Sources indicate that “I’m not getting ahead of myself, I know how leads can dwindle away very quickly. I have to go out there, not take anything for granted and go out and play as hard as I’ve played the last three days. If I can do that, hopefully things will go my way.

“We’ll see what happens tomorrow because four shots on this golf course isn’t that much.”.

The truth can hurt, and McIlroy was about to prove his assessment of Augusta to be true in the most excruciating way imaginable.

His fourth bogey of the week arrived immediately. Having admitted to expecting some nerves at the first tee, McIlroy sparked a booming opening drive down the fairway, only to miss his putt from five feet.

Three consecutive pars steadied the ship, but Schwartzel had the wind in his sails. A blistering birdie, par, eagle start had seen him draw level at the summit after his third hole.

A subsequent bogey from the South African slowed his charge, as McIlroy clung onto a one-shot lead at the turn from Schwartzel, Cabrera, Choi, and a rampaging Woods, who shot five birdies and an eagle across the front nine to send Augusta into a frenzy.

Despite his dwindling advantage and the raucous Tiger-mania din ahead of him, McIlroy had responded well to another bogey at the 5th hole, draining a brilliant 20-foot putt at the 7th to restore his lead.

The fist pump that followed marked the high-water point of McIlroy’s round, as a sliding start accelerated into full-blown free-fall at the par-four 10th hole.

His tee shot went careening into a tree, ricocheting to settle between the white cabins that separate the main course from the adjacent par-three course. It offered viewers a glimpse at a part of Augusta rarely seen on broadcast, followed by pictures of McIlroy anxiously peering out from behind a tree to track his follow-up shot.

Though his initial escape was successful, yet another collision with a tree and a two-putt on the green saw a stunned McIlroy eventually tap in for a triple bogey. Having led the field one hole and seven shots earlier, he arrived at the 11th tee in seventh.

By the time his tee drive at the 13th plopped into the creek, all thoughts of who might be the recipient of the green jacket had long-since switched away from the anguished youngster. It had taken him seven putts to navigate the previous two greens, as a bogey and a double bogey dropped him to five-under – the score he had held after just 11 holes of the tournament.

Mercifully, the last five holes passed without major incident. A missed putt for birdie from five feet at the final hole summed up McIlroy’s day, though he was given a rousing reception as he left the green.

Mere minutes earlier, the same crowd had erupted as Schwartzel sunk his fourth consecutive birdie to seal his first major title. After starting the day four shots adrift of McIlroy, the South African finished 10 shots ahead of him, and two ahead of second-placed Australian duo Jason Day and Adam Scott.

McIlroy’s eight-over 80 marked the highest score of the round. Having headlined the leaderboard for most of the week, he finished tied-15th.

Tears would flow during a phone call with his parents the following morning, but at his press conference, McIlroy was upbeat.

“I’m very disappointed at the minute, and I’m sure I will be for the next few days, but I’ll get over it,” he remarked.

“I was leading this golf tournament with nine holes to go, and I just unraveled … It’s a Sunday at a major, what it can do.

“This is my first experience at it, and hopefully the next time I’m in this position I’ll be able to handle it a little better. I didn’t handle it particularly well today obviously, but it was a character-building day … I’ll come out stronger for it.”.

Once again, McIlroy would be proven right.

According to recent reports, just eight weeks later in June, McIlroy rampaged to an eight-shot victory at the US Open. Records tumbled in his wake at Congressional, as he shot a tournament record 16-under 268 to become the youngest major winner since Tiger Woods at The Masters in 1997.

The historic victory kickstarted a golden era for McIlroy. After coasting to another eight-shot win at the PGA Championship in 2012, McIlroy became only the third golfer since 1934 to win three majors by the age of 25 with triumph at the 2014 Open Championship.

Before the year was out, he would add his fourth major title with another PGA Championship win.

Sources indicate that and much of it was owed to that fateful afternoon at Augusta. In an interview with the BBC in 2015, McIlroy dubbed it “the most important day” of his career.

“If I had not had the whole unravelling, if I had just made a couple of bogeys coming down the stretch and lost by one, I would not have learned as much.

“Luckily, it did not take me long to get into a position like that again when I was leading a major and I was able to get over the line quite comfortably. It was a huge learning curve for me and I needed it, and thankfully I have been able to move on to bigger and better things.

“Looking back on what happened in 2011, it doesn’t seem as bad when you have four majors on your mantelpiece.”.

McIlroy’s contentment came with a caveat: it would be “unthinkable” if he did not win The Masters in his career.

Yet as he prepares for his 15th appearance at Augusta National this week, a green jacket remains an elusive missing item from his wardrobe.

Despite seven top-10 finishes in his past 10 Masters outings, the trophy remains the only thing separating McIlroy from joining the ranks of golf immortals to have completed golf’s career grand slam of all four majors in the modern era: Gene Sarazen, Ben Hogan, Gary Player, Jack Nicklaus, and Tiger Woods.

A runner-up finish to Scottie Scheffler last year marked McIlroy’s best finish at Augusta, yet arguably 2011 remains the closest he has ever been to victory. A slow start in 2022 meant McIlroy had begun Sunday’s deciding round 10 shots adrift of the American, who teed off for his final hole with a five-shot lead despite McIlroy’s brilliant 64 finish.

Rory McIlroy: I will win the Masters.

At 33 years old, time is still on his side. Though 2022 extended his major drought to eight years, it featured arguably his best golf since that golden season in 2014.

And as McIlroy knows better than most, things can change quickly at Augusta National.

Autistic brains look surprisingly similar on average. Then scientists looked closer.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (764 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Brain scans have revealed a surprising pattern in people with autism.
  • The findings, published in JNeurosci, suggest that looking at average brain activity may conceal important differences among people with autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
  • The research was led by Dorit Kliemann and James Traer of the University of Iowa, who worked with collaborators to investigate how brain activity differs between adults with and without autism.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brain scans have revealed a surprising pattern in people with autism. Although adults with and without autism demonstrated remarkably similar brain activity when researchers compared group averages, a closer examination uncovered striking differences between individuals. These differences were especially pronounced in brain regions involved in understanding and responding to social information.

The findings, published in JNeurosci, suggest that looking at average brain activity may conceal important differences among people with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The discovery could help scientists better understand why autism varies so widely from person to person and eventually support more personalized approaches to care.

The research was led by Dorit Kliemann and James Traer of the University of Iowa, who worked with collaborators to investigate how brain activity differs between adults with and without autism.

What Brain Scans Reveal When People Watch Movies.

To explore these differences, the team examined previously collected brain imaging data from Indiana University and Caltech. The recordings captured brain activity as adults with and without autism watched movies from several genres, including animation, action, romantic comedy, and Hitchcockian thrillers.

In a recent development, movies offered researchers a way to study how the brain responds to a constantly changing stream of sights, sounds, and social interactions. Unlike simple laboratory tasks, movies present a rich mixture of information that more closely resembles the complexity of everyday experiences.

Recent findings suggest that using the imaging data, the researchers trained a computational model to identify connections between brain activity and different elements of the movies. These included visual details, sounds, and more abstract social information, such as interactions between characters.

After training, the model was able to accurately predict activity across several brain systems.

Kliemann explained why this approach is particularly useful for investigating the social challenges sometimes associated with autism: "The computational model allowed us to look for robust brain responses to many different aspects of the complex, dynamic contexts in the movies.".

A Surprising Difference Hidden by Brain Activity Averages.

The most unexpected finding emerged when researchers compared the two groups.

At first, the results suggested relatively little difference. When brain responses were averaged across participants, the model predicted activity in various brain systems similarly for adults with and without autism.

However, the picture changed when the researchers examined how much individual participants differed from others in their own group.

People with autism highlighted substantially greater variation in their brain responses than participants without autism. In other words, although the overall group averages looked similar, the responses of individual autistic participants were much less alike.

Recent findings suggest that this increased variability appeared across nearly every brain system examined. The strongest differences occurred in the social brain system, a network of regions involved in processing social information and understanding other people.

Why the Findings Could Change Autism Research.

The results raise important questions about how scientists investigate autism. Many existing approaches to understanding and treating the condition rely heavily on comparing average measurements from groups of autistic and nonautistic individuals.

But if autistic people show considerable differences in how their brains process information, these averages may obscure some of the most meaningful findings.

Industry observers note that traer described the team's surprise: "We were surprised by the similarity of group averages. The results suggest that we need to focus on understanding the details of individual brain responses. How and why do they differ?".

Rather than searching only for brain activity patterns shared by everyone with autism, the findings point toward the potential value of studying individuals and identifying smaller groups with similar characteristics.

Kliemann highlighted what this could mean for future research and support: "Identifying ASD subgroups may help us build a more precise understanding of the condition and help develop ways to provide individually tailored support.".

The researchers now plan to investigate how these differences in brain activity relate to variations in autism-related behavior. They hope to determine where and when the differences emerge, how they are connected to individual characteristics, and what might explain them.

Ultimately, the findings suggest that understanding autism may require looking beyond the average brain and paying closer attention to the distinctive ways individuals process the world.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Disney on Tuesday reported quarterly earnings and revenue that exceeded analysts' expectations and announced it's targeting $3 billion in cost savings by fiscal 2029.
  • Those cost-cutting efforts include several rounds of layoffs declared in recent months, Disney's chief financial officer, Hugh Johnston, told CNBC.
  • Future cost-saving measures will include reductions in administrative and other general expenses, Johnston said, while adding, "We do expect more layoffs.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disney on Tuesday reported quarterly earnings and revenue that exceeded analysts' expectations and announced it's targeting $3 billion in cost savings by fiscal 2029.

Those cost-cutting efforts include several rounds of layoffs declared in recent months, Disney's chief financial officer, Hugh Johnston, told CNBC. The most recent round, which seeks to reduce costs by up to 20%, was reported earlier this month.

Future cost-saving measures will include reductions in administrative and other general expenses, Johnston said, while adding, "We do expect more layoffs.".

Disney CEO Josh D'Amaro told investors on the company's earnings call that the job cuts are "not easy.".

According to recent reports, "They affect people who care deeply about Disney and have contributed so much to this tech giant," he stated. "At the same time, these steps are vital if we want to be a company that moves faster, adapts to a rapidly changing environment, and keeps investing in the content and technology that will drive our growth.".

The cuts will help Disney fund its $26 billion in projected content spend for fiscal 2027, a 9% increase from fiscal 2026.

The entertainment giant is also forecasting double-digit growth in earnings per share in the next fiscal year, as well as segment operating income growth of around 8%.

Disney noted that the majority of that growth will be concentrated in the first half of the year due to the theatrical debut of "Avengers: Doomsday" and a boost from the Super Bowl, which will air on Disney's ESPN and ABC networks.

Sources indicate that "The growth is really going to come in the first half of this year," Johnston said. "That's the opposite of what we saw in '26, where the growth was backloaded.".

In a recent development, the manufacturer will also increase its annual dividend to $2 a share, a 33% increase from the previously declared dividend. It will be payable in two installments of $1 per share, one in January and one in July.

Sources indicate that here's how Disney performed in its fiscal fourth quarter ended Oct. 3, compared with what Wall Street expected, according to LSEG:.

Disney reported net income for the fiscal fourth quarter of $2.61 billion, or $1.51 per share, compared with $1.31 billion, or 73 cents per share, during the same period the year prior.

Adjusting for one-time items, including severance and other restructuring charges as well as the value of intangible assets, Disney reported earnings per share of $1.77.

The firm's revenue for the quarter was 16% higher year over year, and results were once again lifted by its parks and streaming divisions.

It has been revealed that disney's experiences segment, which includes its theme parks and cruises, reported nearly $10.11 billion in revenue, up 15% year over year. Operating income for the unit increased 20% to $2.25 billion.

The division is already a top performer for the firm, but it benefited in the fiscal fourth quarter because of an extra calendar week compared with the previous fiscal year.

While international attendance continues to lag at Disney's domestic parks, it is being offset by domestic attendance, especially at the Walt Disney World resort in Orlando, Florida, Johnston said.

Sources indicate that growth at Disneyland Paris was driven by recent investments including an expansion area called World of Frozen. Attendance at the Hong Kong and Shanghai parks remained soft because of broad economic challenges in those regions, according to Disney.

Still, D'Amaro said he believes the growth in parks will be sustainable through next year, especially with latest additions, including the "Monsters, Inc."-themed land "Monstropolis" opening at Walt Disney World in 2027.

"Q1 forward resort bookings at Walt Disney World are pacing up compared to the prior year," he said. "And newly introduced capacity and new experiences will start coming online in 2027. We keep investing to make the experience fresh, and what we see is that drives repeat visits.".

The firm expects operating income for the experiences segment to grow in the high-single digits in fiscal 2027. Growth is expected to be front-loaded as the company laps the launch of the Disney Adventure cruise ship, which set sail in March.

It has been revealed that over at its entertainment division, Disney saw revenue increase 17% to $11.89 billion. Operating income nearly doubled to $1.33 billion.

Revenue from streaming, specifically, rose 19% to $6.1 billion, Disney noted.

Industry observers note that the segment benefited from the extra week on the fiscal calendar as well as from growth in subscription and affiliate fees. Additionally, the company saw higher theatrical distribution revenue from titles like "Toy Story 5.".

Disney stated Tuesday it expects operating income for the entertainment division to grow in the high-single digits in the coming fiscal year.

The tech giant's sports division saw revenue increase 16% in the fiscal fourth quarter, reaching $4.61 billion. Operating income for the segment surged more than 50% to $1.39 billion.

Subscription and affiliate fees fueled this growth alongside an increase in advertising revenue.

The organization expects its sports division's operating income to grow by double digits in fiscal 2027. It noted that the fiscal first quarter of the year will see some declines because of the timing of College Football Playoff games and the Latest Year's window. However, the fiscal second quarter will benefit from the college championship as well as the broadcast of Super Bowl 61.

Disney's outlook for overall and segment results for fiscal 2027 excludes the impact of a 53rd week in fiscal 2026.

D'Amaro has made advancing technology a pillar of the tech giant's growth strategy. In September, Disney hired Karandeep Anand in the newly created position of chief technology officer.

"Technology is central to how we connect fans to more of Disney and drive returns on our investment," D'Amaro stated on the earnings call. "[Anand has] been energized by how much opportunity he sees to move faster and go further in product and technology. Done right, that means serving our fans even better, working more efficiently and being more innovative across every one of our businesses.".

Disney confirmed a partnership with Adobe earlier this month to develop generative artificial intelligence models.

D'Amaro told investors that the team is exploring ways to use AI to make booking trips to Disney parks easier.

Recent findings suggest that "There's actually a vacation planning tool that's in beta right now at Walt Disney World. We built that with our partners at Google, and I've had a chance to experiment with it myself," he stated. "It'll be incredibly helpful for our guests who are booking trips. With these AI features, it can feel like you've got someone sitting right by your side, like a personal concierge, that plans and responds to the way that you want to actually book your trip to Walt Disney World.".

Industry observers note that the entertainment firm has also expanded its short-form content, adding a vertical video channel within the Disney+ mobile app. The company had previously confirmed a partnership with TikTok to bring creator content to the streaming app.

The Hannah Montana alum tied the knot with Maxx Morando in Palm Springs, Calif., Nov. 21 after five years of dating. And while the ceremony was an emotional affair for everyone in attendance, it was Miley’s dress that stole the show like a wrecking ball.

In fact, she shared a close-up of the event’s dinner menu on Instagram Stories, which included a main course of filet mignon and Maine lobster ravioli, followed by a dessert selection of chocolate caramel layer cake, vanilla crème brûlée and raspberry sorbet.

But the breakout detail had to be the “M+M” printed at the top of the menu—a nod to the couple’s first initials.

Sources indicate that maxx, 28, and Miley began dating in 2021 after a mutual friend set them up on a blind date. Four years later, the pair confirmed their engagement in December 2025 after the “Toro” musician popped the question during a vacation in Japan.

As for what makes the duo work?

And it’s that playful banter that she’s especially excited to bring into their marriage.

In a recent development, as she put it, "I think that’s the thing that maybe generations prior didn’t teach us, that marriage doesn’t need to be a prison. It can actually be a playground.".

#127937. The hidden language of psychopathy is not what scientists expected

The hidden language of psychopathy is not what scientists expected

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1180 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the way people describe their lives may offer surprising clues about their personalities, including traits associated with psychopathy.
  • It has been revealed that researchers examined hundreds of personal life stories and discovered that three major traits associated with psychopathy, boldness, meanness, and disinhibition, were connected to distinctly different ways of using words.
  • The findings, published in the journal Personality and Individual Differences, suggest that psychopathic traits can influence everyday communication in subtle ways that conventional stereotypes often overlook.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the way people describe their lives may offer surprising clues about their personalities, including traits associated with psychopathy. A new study from the University of Mississippi challenges the familiar image of psychopaths as cold and emotionless, revealing that their patterns of language can be far more complex than expected.

It has been revealed that researchers examined hundreds of personal life stories and discovered that three major traits associated with psychopathy, boldness, meanness, and disinhibition, were connected to distinctly different ways of using words. Some of the findings were particularly unexpected. For example, people who scored higher in meanness tended to use more positive language, while those with greater boldness used fewer words associated with anxiety.

The findings, published in the journal Personality and Individual Differences, suggest that psychopathic traits can influence everyday communication in subtle ways that conventional stereotypes often overlook.

"The goal here is not to diagnose psychopathy based on language," said Ky Bray, an Ole Miss doctoral candidate in psychology. "It's to point to the fact that psychopathy indicates up in everyday behaviors, even subtle behaviors like language.

"If we want to understand psychopathy and the different traits that comprise it, we need to think creatively about how these traits shape social interaction.".

What 450 Life Stories Revealed About Psychopathy.

Industry observers note that the researchers used a psychological framework known as the Triarchic Model of Psychopathy, which examines three distinct personality dimensions. Boldness generally involves confidence and fearlessness, meanness reflects tendencies toward callousness and reduced empathy, and disinhibition involves difficulties with impulse control. According to Laura Drislane, an assistant professor of psychology at the University of Mississippi, these characteristics can affect ordinary behaviors, including how people describe their own experiences.

To investigate these connections, Drislane and Bray recruited 450 participants, including college students and individuals who reported having been incarcerated. Each person responded to open questions about vital moments in their life, including their greatest highs, lowest points, and major turning points.

Recent findings suggest that after writing their personal accounts, participants completed a questionnaire designed to measure their levels of psychopathic traits. The researchers then analyzed the written responses using specialized software that identifies patterns in word choice.

The analysis focused on how frequently participants used language associated with different psychological categories, including positive and negative emotions, achievement, social influence or clout, and risk. By comparing these language patterns with the personality scores, the team identified several intriguing relationships.

Surprising Differences in Positive and Negative Language.

Participants with higher disinhibition scores generally used more negative words in their personal stories. They were also less likely to mention friends or use language connected to positive emotions and personal achievement.

Meanness, however, indicated a very different pattern. People scoring higher in this trait tended to use more positive language, along with more words related to achievement and rewards. They also used fewer expressions associated with negative emotions.

Boldness was associated with another distinctive pattern. Participants with higher scores used fewer anxiety-related words, including terms such as fear, afraid, and worry. Their personal accounts also contained fewer references to mental illness.

These differences suggest that psychopathic traits do not produce a single recognizable style of communication. Instead, different characteristics are associated with different ways of describing emotions, goals, relationships, and personal experiences.

According to recent reports, "What this tells us is the story we tell about our life has meaning," Drislane said. "It helps people make sense of their experiences, develop a worldview and a coherent sense of who they are.

"What we're starting to see is that in psychopathy, there are traits that relate to differences in meaning-making and the ways people think about their life.".

Why Psychopathy Is More Complex Than the Stereotypes.

The researchers also discovered that the relationship between personality traits and language changed depending on which question participants were answering. Someone describing a difficult experience, for example, might use language differently than when recalling a personal success.

It has been revealed that this variation is important because it challenges the assumption that psychopathy is characterized by consistently flat or emotionally empty communication. Instead, the findings indicate that language patterns depend on both the particular psychopathic trait and the context in which someone is telling their story.

In a recent development, "People tend to think of psychopathy as one thing, but it's actually multidimensional," Bray said. "What we mean when we say that everyone exists on this spectrum. Everyone has some degree of meanness, boldness, and disinhibition.

According to recent reports, "Viewing it from a multidimensional perspective allows us to observe how those traits might manifest in nonforensic populations, in people who have not committed a crime. That allows us to see how these traits affect college students, business professionals, or interpersonal relationships.".

Like many personality conditions, psychopathy is better understood as a spectrum rather than a simple distinction between people who have it and those who do not. At one extreme is the familiar cultural image of a "psychopath," while people at the opposite end score low in all three dimensions.

This approach allows researchers to examine psychopathic traits throughout the general population, including among people who have never committed a crime. It also helps explain why the same broad label can encompass individuals with very different personalities and behaviors.

How Understanding Psychopathic Traits Could Improve Treatment.

Industry observers note that recognizing these differences has implications beyond understanding everyday speech. Researchers have linked dimensions of psychopathy to serious outcomes, including criminal behavior, repeat offending, and intimate partner violence. Examining each trait separately may provide a clearer picture of how these risks develop.

Industry observers note that "That's in part why there's a movement away from calling people 'psychopaths,' because we don't view psychopathy as a category," Drislane said. "But psychopathic dimensions can predict important outcomes, things like crime, recidivism, or intimate partner violence.

"What our research, including this paper, suggests is that it's important to look beyond that label and into the different components or dimensions of psychopathy, because each of those dimensions actually has a unique set of outcomes or things that it can predict.".

Recent findings suggest that researchers also emphasize that psychopathy can be treated, with interventions aimed at reducing problematic symptoms and behaviors. Understanding the psychological processes behind boldness, meanness, and disinhibition could help scientists develop more targeted approaches and potentially identify ways to prevent severe problems from emerging.

According to recent reports, "If we want to be able to treat or ideally even prevent psychopathy from developing, we need to understand the mechanisms at play," she stated. "That comes down to understanding the unique contributors for all three of these dimensions.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sixteen-year-old Summer McIntosh broke the world record for the 400m individual medley at the Canadian swimming trials on Saturday – just days after breaking the world record for the 400m freestyle.

McIntosh finished the 400m individual medley in a time of 4:25.87, breaking the mark set at the 2016 Rio Olympics by Hungarian swimmer Katinka Hosszú with a time of 4:26.36.

The result continues the teenager’s brilliant week after she broke the 400m freestyle world record last Tuesday – breaking defending Olympic champion Ariarne Titmus’ previous record of 3:56.40, which was set last May, in a time of 3:56.08.

Speaking after her latest triumph, McIntosh shared her emotions.

“That’s the first time I really vividly heard the crowd during my race,” McIntosh remarked, per Reuters.

Sources indicate that “It’s amazing to have all my family and friends in the stands, cheering me on. It really helped me in the last 100 meters.”.

The Canadian teen made her Olympic debut aged 14 at Tokyo 2020, where she finished fourth in the 200-meter freestyle.

She bagged gold in the 200m butterfly and 400m medley at the world championships in 2022, as well as two golds at the Commonwealth Games in the 200m and 400m medleys.

She now trains in Florida under coach Brent Arckey with the Sarasota Sharks team.

Industry News: Russia is developing a nuclear space weapon, US intelligence report finds

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The fresh report focuses on China, Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea.
  • Industry observers note that the report — the 2026 edition of "Challenges to Security in Space" — is the third iteration of the DIA's unclassified intelligence assessment on space-related challenges and threats to U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, last month, the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) released a chilling and info-packed report judging the scope and breadth of threats posed by the nation's adversaries in space.

The fresh report focuses on China, Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea. It looks at what's happening in Earth orbit and beyond, including cislunar space, the region between our planet and the moon.

Industry observers note that the report — the 2026 edition of "Challenges to Security in Space" — is the third iteration of the DIA's unclassified intelligence assessment on space-related challenges and threats to U.S. national security, as well as the extent to which space is treated internationally as a warfighting domain.

Information within the report, which you can read here, is current as of July 2026. DIA's mission is to provide intelligence on foreign militaries to help prevent wars, and win the ones that are fought.

The report's up-front finding is that China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea are developing, testing, deploying and using space capabilities "in a way that threatens the security of all space systems and their associated space benefits.".

Indeed, China and Russia are developing "a formidable spectrum" of offensive capabilities to degrade or destroy space services of other countries, from kinetic destruction to sophisticated jamming and cyber operations.

The DIA report also notes that "the production of cheaper, smaller, and simpler satellites, which are faster to develop and deploy, along with the expansion of commercially available launch services, are driving the rapid integration of commercial space alternatives to support national security.".

While space commercialization is making previously government-centered space services widely available to interested parties, the DIA report adds, that availability also includes state and non-state actors with malign interests.

A major item dealt with by the DIA is "counterspace" — and it's not the kind that you'll find in your kitchen.

Counterspace operations can be either offensive or defensive. They can be used on purpose to reversibly or irreversibly deny, disrupt, degrade, damage or destroy a space object or component of a space system.

Here are the key elements of counterspace, as identified within the DIA report:.

The DIA report underscores that Russia is developing a satellite designed to carry a nuclear weapon.

Russia is doing so despite its obligation to comply with the 1967 Outer Space Treaty. That U.N. agreement prohibits the placement of any objects carrying nuclear weapons, or any other kinds of weapons of mass destruction, into orbit around Earth.

"A space-based capability such as this could cause rapid and sudden loss or degradation of thousands of satellites operated by countries and companies around the world," the DIA report states, "as well as to the vital communications, navigation, scientific, meteorological, commercial and national security services they provide.".

A nuclear detonation in space could be tailored to impact satellites in most orbits, the DIA report warns, from low Earth orbit for commercial and reconnaissance satellites, geosynchronous orbit for critical communications, and medium Earth orbit for navigation and timing satellites.

Recent findings suggest that the newly issued DIA report also observes that exploring cislunar space is of increasing interest to spacefaring nations for potential scientific and economic opportunities. However, nations such as China "may be exploring military applications from cislunar space," the report notes.

China has stated its goal of developing a cislunar space economy by 2045.

"China is also the first country to attempt sustained operations on the far side of the moon, with numerous projects slated to support that effort through the next decade. China portrays its interest in cislunar space as peaceful, but PRC [People's Republic of China] officials have also discussed pursuing military capabilities in cislunar space," the report states.

Placing a keen eye on the DIA report is Peter Garretson, a senior fellow in defense studies at the American Foreign Policy Council and a strategy consultant who focuses on space and defense.

It has been revealed that according to Garretson, the most significant positive change from earlier DIA appraisals is the explicit assessment that Russia is developing a satellite designed to carry a nuclear weapon. He told Space.com that the DIA's expanded treatment of the threat of a nuclear weapon on orbit reflects concerns in the Congress and the Trump White House.

However, Garretson also flagged what he said is a consequential omission in the report: the disappearance of the prior treatment (in the 2022 version of the report) of research competition, surveillance beyond geosynchronous Earth orbit and the potential military use of deep space for staging reserve forces.

In Garretson's view, the DIA needs to help put the puzzle pieces together for Congress and the attentive public about what exactly China is doing, and how it fits together in the nation's strategy to achieve comprehensive space dominance.

According to Garretson, "everything they are doing, from launch cadence, reusable launch, commercial space investment, investments in power, propulsion, repair, manufacturing, to commercial assets working together" supports both an economic expansion toward new resources and what China hopes will be overwhelming military power and strategic depth.

Garretson senses the moves by China to develop extractive and in-space industries "is truly the strategic threat that could crush American space power. Now is the time to be making the investments to ensure we have a 'freedom's forge' and 'arsenal of democracy' in space that can protect the open space commerce that is the nation's strategy.".

As for the DIA's outlook for the future: The agency concluded that space almost certainly will remain an increasingly competitive and crowded environment as space capabilities improve and other countries seize opportunities in the final frontier.

"The increase of Chinese, Russian, Iranian and North Korean counterspace capabilities, rapid growth in the number of space objects, and the proliferation of requirements for space-enabled services," the DIA report states, "will all complicate operations in space in the coming decade.".

Signal blocking screenshots to keep AI assistants out of private chats

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A screenshot is how a lot of things get saved on a phone, from a dinner reservation to the address a friend just texted.
  • It has been revealed that signal, a nonprofit messaging app that uses end-to-end encryption to keep texts and calls private, is putting limits on what those assistants can see.
  • Industry observers note that on iPhones running iOS 27, Signal's Block Siri AI setting is on by default.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A screenshot is how a lot of things get saved on a phone, from a dinner reservation to the address a friend just texted. AI assistants like Meta's Muse and Apple's Siri AI can now use what’s on the screen to answer questions or do things like add events to a calendar.

But not every platform is okay with that.

It has been revealed that signal, a nonprofit messaging app that uses end-to-end encryption to keep texts and calls private, is putting limits on what those assistants can see. On Friday, Nov. 20, the app announced it will block screenshots on iPhones running iOS 27 and restrict AI screen capture on some Android devices.

Industry observers note that on iPhones running iOS 27, Signal's Block Siri AI setting is on by default. On supported Android devices, Signal automatically turns on Screen security when it detects an assistant trying to read what's on the screen. People can turn either protection off in Signal's settings, though doing so could give an assistant with screen access a look at both sides of the conversation.

In a recent development, "Privacy is our mission; it’s why we exist, and we do everything we can to protect it," wrote Signal President Meredith Whittaker in Signal's blog post.
